notes: Mardin Airport is 20 minutes from the city. A car is useless in Old Mardin, so walk. For Midyat, Dara and Nusaybin, take a car or minibus.
Order the stuffed ribs (kaburga dolması) in advance at Cercis Murat. Mırra is bitter coffee, and you hand the cup back. Almond candy and terebinth soap make good souvenirs.
In winter, days are mild (10-15°C) and nights are cold. The best season is March to April; snow is rare.
Respect service times at Syriac churches and monasteries. Deyrulzafaran is entered on a guided tour, and short sleeves are not allowed.
The streets of Old Mardin are steep and paved with stone, so wear comfortable shoes and cool off in the abbaralar.
Sunset at Kasımiye is Mardin's most famous sight. Arrive 1 hour early.

stops.name: Zinciriye Medresesi
stops.tips: Mardin's highest madrasa. The domed terrace overlooks the Mesopotamian plain, and mornings are cool.

stops.name: Mardin Grand Mosque
stops.tips: Artuqid minaret, set within the bazaar.

stops.name: Mardin Coppersmiths' Bazaar
stops.tips: Copper, almond candy and Mardin soap. Donkeys still haul goods along the stone lanes.

stops.name: Cercis Murat Konağı
stops.tips: Syriac-Mardin cuisine in a stone mansion with a terrace view. Order the stuffed ribs (kaburga dolması) in advance.

stops.name: Kasımiye Medresesi
stops.tips: A twin-domed madrasa with a courtyard pool. The plain turns red at sunset.

backups.name: Seyr-i Merdin Kafe
backups.tips: Terrace café for coffee and Mardin çöreği (sweet pastry).

backups.name: Mardin Museum
backups.tips: Archaeology museum in the former patriarchate. An indoor alternative to the madrasa.

stops.name: Deyrulzafaran Monastery
stops.tips: A 1,500-year-old Syriac monastery. Take the guided tour to see the sun temple and the patriarchs' tombs. Join the first group in the morning.

stops.name: Kırklar Church
stops.tips: An active Syriac church in Old Mardin with a quiet courtyard.

stops.name: Antik Mardin Sofrası
stops.tips: Ikbebet, sembusek and dobo in a mansion restaurant.

stops.name: Mardin Şahkulubey Konağı
stops.tips: A stone mansion with a courtyard, plus a walk through the bazaar lanes.

stops.name: Mardin Castle Viewpoint
stops.tips: The castle is military, but the viewpoint at its foot is open. Watch the city and plain at sunset.

backups.name: Mardin Kebapçısı Yusuf Usta
backups.tips: Mardin kebab and içli köfte (stuffed bulgur meatballs).

stops.name: Dara Ancient City
stops.tips: 30 km from Mardin. Roman cistern, necropolis and rock tombs, known as the 'Ephesus of Mesopotamia'.

stops.name: Dara Village Breakfast
stops.tips: Mardin breakfast in a village house, with dövme cheese (crushed-olive cheese) and bulgur with eggs.

stops.name: Savur
stops.tips: A stone town nicknamed Little Mardin, with a castle, mansions and mulberry orchards.

stops.name: Savur Kahveci Konağı
stops.tips: Mırra (bitter coffee) and mulberry molasses in a mansion.

backups.name: Kızıltepe Grand Mosque
backups.tips: An Artuqid mosque. An alternative to Savur.

stops.name: Midyat Konukevi
stops.tips: The mansion from the TV series Sıla, with a terrace and fine stonework. 1 hour from Midyat.

stops.name: Midyat Old Bazaar
stops.tips: Telkâri (silver filigree) masters and Syriac wine.

stops.name: Mor Barsavmo Church
stops.tips: Midyat's active Syriac church.

stops.name: Midyat Kasr-ı Nehroz Restaurant
stops.tips: Syriac cuisine in a stone mansion: perde pilavı (pilaf baked in pastry) and alluciye.

stops.name: Mor Gabriel Monastery
stops.tips: One of the world's oldest active monasteries (397). Take the guided tour to see the mosaics. 20 km from Midyat.

backups.name: Hasankeyf
backups.tips: New Hasankeyf and the castle. An alternative to Mor Gabriel (1 hour).

stops.name: Mor Yakup Church Nusaybin
stops.tips: A 4th-century church and the excavation of the School of Nisibis, on the Syrian border.

stops.name: Nusaybin Zeynel Abidin Mosque
stops.tips: A tomb and mosque next to the church.

stops.name: Nusaybin Çarşı Lokantası
stops.tips: A town restaurant serving ribs and pilaf.

stops.name: Gırnavaz Mound
stops.tips: An Assyrian mound near Nusaybin, now an excavation site.

backups.name: Mardin Dara Road Viewpoint
backups.tips: Views over the plain. An alternative to the mound.

stops.name: Mardin Soap Workshop
stops.tips: Watch terebinth (bıttım) soap being made, and shop.

stops.name: Mardin Protestant Church
stops.tips: A restored church, now a cultural centre.

stops.name: Mardin Abbaralar
stops.tips: Vaulted lanes running beneath the houses, with cool passages.

stops.name: Mardin Leyli Kahvaltı
stops.tips: Mardin breakfast with clotted cream and honey, and sembusek (savoury pastry).

stops.name: Mardin Şehidiye Medresesi
stops.tips: A madrasa with a minaret and a tea garden. Come at sunset.

backups.name: Latifiye Mosque
backups.tips: An Artuqid mosque. An alternative to Şehidiye.

stops.name: Mardin Almond Candy Shop
stops.tips: Almond candy, Mardin soap and telkâri (silver filigree) souvenirs.

stops.name: Mardin 1st Street
stops.tips: Old Mardin's main street. Take a last walk.

stops.name: Mardin Kahvaltı Konağı
stops.tips: Farewell breakfast on the terrace.

backups.name: Mardin Maristan Kafe
backups.tips: A café in a former Artuqid hospital, with mırra and a terrace.

backups.name: Emir Hamamı Mardin
backups.tips: An Artuqid-era hammam. Say goodbye with a scrub and foam massage.
